cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is about to preach to the Israelites. He's setting before them the testimonies, statutes and ordinances, after they've come out of Egypt. Pull up a chair, friend, because Moses has a LOT to say, and he is saying ALL of it.

They're in the valley across the Jordan facing Beth-peor, on land Israel took from two Amorite kings: Sihon, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan. It runs from Aroer on the Arnon Valley all the way to Mount Hermon, plus the Arabah east of the Jordan down to the Sea of the Arabah, and friend, my whole cookie planet would fit in one corner of it.
Then Moses summoned all Israel, not just the front row, EVERYBODY: "Hear, O Israel, the statutes and ordinances that I declare in your hearing this day."

cards.question: Moses doesn't just want Israel to hear these statutes and ordinances. What else does he tell them to do?

answers.text: Learn them and observe them carefully
Talk them over with their elders
Save them for when they cross over

cards.text: Then Moses takes them back to the mountain: "The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb."

cards.question: Moses says God made the covenant at Horeb with their fathers, not with the people standing there today.

cards.text: Not your grandpa's covenant, friend, YOURS. Moses says the LORD spoke with them face to face out of the fire on the mountain.

cards.question: God is speaking out of the fire on the mountain, and the people won't go up. Why not?

answers.text: They were afraid of the fire
They were too tired to climb
They were busy packing up camp

cards.question: So Moses says that at that time he was standing ___ the LORD and the people to declare to them the word of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses passes on God's words, and God opens with who He is: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery." Friend, when somebody pulls you out of the dark, you LISTEN to whatever they say next.

cards.question: Here's the first command from the God who brought Israel out of Egypt. What does He say about other gods?

answers.text: They must have no other gods before Him
They may honor other gods in other lands
They must keep other gods outside the camp

cards.text: Next, no idols in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath. Sky, ground, sea, God covered EVERY department.

cards.question: God says Israel must not bow down to idols or worship them.
God gives His reason: He, the LORD their God, is a ___ God.

cards.text: God says He visits the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Him. Heavy, friend, but hang on, there's another side.

cards.question: For those who love God and keep His commandments, how far does His loving devotion reach?

cards.text: Then God speaks about His name: they shall not take the name of the LORD their God in vain. Friend, the Millers CARVED my name into my handle, so trust me, a name is a big deal.

cards.question: God says the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.

cards.text: Next up, the Sabbath: "Observe the Sabbath day by keeping it holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you." Friend, I lay in a junk drawer for YEARS doing nothing, and I still never got an official day off.

cards.question: God lays out the week: ___ days to labor and do all their work, and the ___ day is a Sabbath to the LORD their God.
On the Sabbath, who must not do any work?

answers.text: Only the head of each household
Only the men who work the fields

cards.text: Sons, daughters, servants, the foreigner, even the ox and the donkey get the day. Somewhere an ox is hitting the snooze button, and NOBODY can say a word to him.

cards.question: God says the manservant and maidservant get the Sabbath so they may rest just as their masters do.
God tells Israel what to remember as the reason for keeping the Sabbath. What is it?

answers.text: They were slaves and He brought them out
Their fathers rested by the Jordan
The elders asked for a holy day

cards.text: Then comes the command about home: "Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you..." And this one comes with something attached.

cards.question: What comes attached to honoring your father and your mother?

answers.text: A promise of long days in the land
A promise of a double portion
A promise of a seat at the gate

cards.text: Now they come short and sharp: "You shall not murder." "You shall not commit adultery." I shared a drawer with instruction manuals for years, friend, and not ONE of them got to the point like this.

cards.question: The next command is about what belongs to someone else. What is it?
Then one about telling the truth: they shall not bear false witness against their ___.

cards.text: The last one isn't about doing something, it's about wanting: "You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife." Friend, this command goes straight for your heart's shopping cart.

cards.question: God says Israel must not covet anything that belongs to their neighbor.

cards.text: Moses reminds them how it went: the LORD spoke these commandments in a loud voice to the whole assembly, out of the fire, the cloud and the deep darkness on the mountain. Friend, I spent years in the dark of a junk drawer, and the loudest voice in there was a dead battery swearing it still had a little charge left.

cards.question: Once God had spoken those commandments to the assembly, what did He add?
Moses says God wrote the commandments on two tablets of ___ and gave them to him.

cards.text: When the people heard the voice out of the darkness, with the mountain blazing with fire, the heads of the tribes and the elders came to Moses. Friend, I know that moment: every time light hit our junk drawer, we ALL held our breath.

cards.question: Moses reminds Israel what they told him that day: they had seen that a man can live even if God speaks with him.
Israel heard God's voice out of the fire and lived. So what do they fear will happen if they keep hearing it?

answers.text: The great fire will consume them
The mountain will fall on them

cards.text: They ask Moses: who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the fire, like they have, and survived? Friend, when you make it through something like that, you do NOT ask for an encore.

cards.question: So they ask Moses to go near, hear God out and pass it all on to them. And they promise they will ___ and ___.

cards.text: The LORD heard every word the people spoke to Moses. And He has something to say about it.

cards.question: God is unhappy with what the people said to Moses.

cards.text: Then God says, "If only they had such a heart to fear Me and keep all My commandments always..." I bet you can hear the longing in that, friend.

cards.question: Why does God wish the people had that kind of heart?

answers.text: So it would go well with them and their children
So He wouldn't need to speak out of the fire
So the nations would hear about Israel

cards.text: Then God tells Moses to send the people back to their tents. Meeting's over, go on home.

cards.question: God tells Moses to head back to his tent with everyone else.

cards.text: Moses stays so God can speak to him all the commandments, statutes and ordinances he's to teach them for the land. Then Moses brings it home: "So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you..."

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to be careful to do what God commanded. What does he say about turning aside from it?

answers.text: They must not turn aside at all
They may turn aside if the elders agree
They may turn aside once they settle

cards.question: Moses says walking in all God's ways is so they may live and prosper and prolong their days in the land.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Moses is just getting warmed up, and trust me, this oven is nowhere near done.
